checks.label: When two variables are directly proportional they increase at the same rate: if the first is doubled, the other is also doubled. 100 V, 200 V and 400 V on a 10 : 1 transformer give 10 V, 20 V and 40 V, and wherever the mark is dragged, twice the primary gives twice the secondary

The turns ratio of any given transformer will be the same as its voltage ratio, so on a 10 : 1 transformer 230 V on the primary gives 230 ÷ 10 = 23 V, a rise of 100 V on the primary is a rise of 10 V on the secondary, and 11.5 V on the secondary needs 11.5 × 10 = 115 V

A fixed charge plus a rate rises steadily but is not in direct proportion: £40 plus £30 an hour costs £40 at 0 hours and £30 more each hour, and for every whole number of hours from 1 to 10, twice the hours costs £40 less than twice the bill, the call-out paid once; so 2 hours at £100 to 4 hours at £160 is × 2 on the hours but × 1.6 on the cost

Only Firm B is in direct proportion: it charges £0 at 0 hours and twice as much for twice the hours (£35, £70, £105); Firms A (£45, £80, £115) and C (£60, £90, £120) rise by the same amount each hour but work back to £10 and £30 at 0 hours, so twice the hours does not cost twice as much

Taking the fixed part off leaves an amount in proportion: 5 hours cost £40 + 5 × £30 = £190; 50 m of cable on a 3 kg drum weighing 8 kg is 5 kg of cable, so 100 m on it weigh 3 + 2 × 5 = 13 kg; the van hire's 2 extra days cost £145 − £85 = £60, so a day is £30, the fee £85 − £60 = £25, and 6 days £25 + 6 × £30 = £205

Each puzzle accepts only its own answer, worked out by its rule, and every wrong answer offered is the one a named slip gives: the ratio read backwards, the gap between its parts kept as if adding, the same rise on both scales, the rise × 10, a whole bill scaled with its fixed part, the fixed part left out, two bills added so the fixed part is paid twice, or a firm whose price rises steadily but has a fixed part

The two scales stay locked: wherever the mark can be dragged, from 0 to 400 V in steps of 10 V, its dots on both lines sit at the same point and its labels read the primary's voltage and a tenth of it, 0 V over 0 V at the left

Every picture is drawn to scale, finished: each row of blocks is its fixed part and one block for each hour, day or 50 m, as long as its total and tagged with it, the doubled bill with two call-outs; each table and scale shows the amounts the working gives

Before an answer, nothing in a puzzle's picture shows its answer: no cell, label or tag gives the missing voltage, its step, the secondary's rise or its reading at 300 V, a total asked for, a firm's price at 0 hours, or the worth of a block still to be found, and no working is written

Every demonstration has finished arriving within 3 to 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion within 2.5 s; parts start at least 0.45 s apart, each once the travel before it has ended; a counted travel holds each voltage at least 0.2 s
